scenario: A recruiter creates one personal two-action Shortcut, assigns it to a supported iPhone Action Button, captures an authorized conversation screenshot in place, and later reviews, discards, or explicitly advances the local evidence without silent Agent processing.
frozen_evidence: artifact-r7.md with 15 matching SHA-256 source hashes

review_plan.reason: Evaluate first-time setup burden, interruption recovery, and whether the capture wedge helps a time-constrained independent recruiter.
Evaluate screenshot provenance, local privacy, state promotion, identity boundaries, rejection ordering, and reversibility.
Evaluate mobile hierarchy, touch targets, localization, Dynamic Type, status legibility, and recovery.
Evaluate candidate-data trust, purpose limitation, human agency, and avoidance of overclaiming.

findings.criterion: One-time setup burden versus real recruiter fallback
findings.observation: The release candidate now clears the honesty and setup-discipline bar for exposure. It teaches the exact two-action personal Shortcut, names the primary control for what it actually does, keeps generic App Shortcuts separate, and avoids a fake one-tap install claim. It remains a 3 rather than a 4 because the one-time setup burden is proven by aligned simulator evidence, not by first-time recruiter completion on physical Action Button devices.
findings.evidence: artifact-r7.md freezes product commit c43145222c7750bf5cfc705384e46ce694f325df and all 15 listed hashes; I recomputed every listed SHA-256 on 2026-09-04 and all matched. /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-c431452.xcresult reports 26 tests and succeeded. Screenshot 3CCAE38B-A080-47A9-8E02-AA93CEF28919.png shows the recruiter-visible setup loop: Take Screenshot, Review screenshot, Local before you decide, and Open Shortcut editor. Screenshot 9BE3703B-4A2E-41A1-96E3-A75CA7BFD4F0.png shows the entry labeled Set up quick capture with One-time setup. Dimension scores from the r7 evidence: trigger relevance=3, capture burden=3, evidence review=3, state integrity=3, action usefulness=3, write safety=3, interruption recovery=3, wedge discipline=3.
findings.user_impact: A time-constrained independent recruiter can set this up without being misled about what the app or iOS is doing, but the team still lacks direct proof that first-time users finish the setup faster than their existing workaround under live-search interruption.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current setup surface and validate it in the field instead of redesigning it again. Measure first-pass completion, detours into Other shortcuts, and abandonment on physical Action Button devices.
findings.verification: On physical Action Button iPhones, have first-time recruiters start from a fresh install and reach first successful screenshot capture with no coaching. Record completion rate, detours, time-to-first-success, and whether they can restate the Assigned versus Local receipt boundary.

findings.observation: The receipt state is now operationally trustworthy. Local receipt is distinct from Assigned, Screenshot received via Shortcuts explicitly limits what was observed, and the unchecked assignment control stays visible. The recruiter can safely resume on next launch and choose keep or discard before processing. The remaining friction is that the receipt surface still communicates status more than it accelerates the next review step.
findings.evidence: CandidateSignalUITests.swift asserts that with action-button-complete NO and screenshot-shortcut-received-at set, the settings row contains Local receipt, the detail label is Screenshot received via Shortcuts, and Action Button Ready is absent. Screenshot 5638E563-863E-488F-BC6E-5FAA0459495C.png shows the unchecked I've assigned the Shortcut control above the receipt card and the footer saying the receipt does not prove the current Action Button assignment. Screenshot 5B7E88EB-5F57-4D6A-9567-D4DC36EC8184.png shows the preserved keep-or-discard gate before processing, and RelationshipCaptureTests.swift covers queue persistence, exact-retry deduplication, later re-import, deletion, unresolved identity, and retry without repeating the identity decision.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter no longer risks mistaking an app-owned receipt for hardware verification or confirmed state, and their work survives interruption. They may still spend an extra navigation step getting from yes, it arrived to the oldest pending screenshot review.
findings.recommendation: When pending capture count is greater than zero, let the Local receipt state expose one direct Review pending screenshot action without changing the current truth boundary or assignment semantics.
findings.verification: Seed queued screenshots, open the Action Button & Shortcuts surface from the Local receipt state, and verify that a direct review action opens the oldest queued capture, preserves FIFO order, and leaves Assigned unchanged.

strengths: The r7 review packet is genuinely frozen: all listed hashes matched at review time, the immutable product commit resolved to c43145222c7750bf5cfc705384e46ce694f325df, and the cited xcresult bundle directly reports 26 passed tests and 0 failed.

The product tells the truth about platform limits. Only the user assigns the Shortcut in Settings, the app cannot read or change the Action Button binding, and Review screenshot is not advertised as a one-step App Shortcut.

The capture-to-review loop is narrow and recruiter-appropriate: capture one authorized conversation, stage it locally, preserve evidence and reviewed draft, then keep, discard, or explicitly continue to Save and check identity.

The rejection path is materially safer in r7: corrupt, over-25-MiB, and over-80-megapixel input is rejected before both queue persistence and receipt creation, which reduces misleading local receipts and cleanup work.
Chinese AX5 evidence remains aligned with the release candidate, including the setup hierarchy and the separate source-settings entry for Local receipt.
missing_evidence: No connected physical iPhone was available, so current Action Button mapping and physical press remain an explicit evidence boundary rather than a product failure.
No first-time recruiter field study yet shows actual setup completion rate, abandonment rate, or measured time saved versus the recruiter's manual fallback.
The receipt status surface does not yet prove a one-tap jump into the oldest queued review item; the release candidate proves safe resume and keep/discard recovery instead.
open_questions: Do first-time recruiters understand Local receipt immediately, or do some still infer broader Action Button verification before opening the detail?
After physical-device validation, does the Other shortcuts section help discovery or create extra setup detours for recruiters who only want screenshot capture?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: r7 fully closes the prior pre-queue validation and receipt-ordering gap, but the frozen artifact still keeps broader post-save deletion and retraction governance outside this release packet instead of proving the full downstream lifecycle after Save and check identity.
findings.evidence: artifact-r7.md lines 143-144 explicitly state that full post-save deletion/retraction across capture, resource, and wiki records remains a broader lifecycle-governance follow-up. The frozen code and tests prove the local pre-save chain instead: apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipCaptureView.swift:441-445 and 1063-1077 state that reviewed text and source metadata are saved separately from the original image, person binding, compiled wiki, and future actions; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipCaptureStore.swift:86-98 and 185-209 show that downstream capture and identity flows begin only after the human taps Save and check identity; /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-c431452.xcresult contains 26 passing leaf tests for import rejection, review, keep/discard, receipt separation, and UI state, but no end-to-end post-save retraction test for derived reviewed-text, resource, or wiki records.
findings.user_impact: This does not introduce a silent import, silent external write, or wrong-assignment defect in the r7 Action Button capture path, but it leaves a narrower unanswered question about how a recruiter later retracts or supersedes reviewed evidence after intentionally promoting it beyond the local inbox.
findings.recommendation: Ship r7 for the scoped Action Button capture release, and schedule a separate frozen lifecycle audit that inventories every post-save reviewed-capture, identity-case, resource, and compiled-wiki representation with explicit delete, supersession, and audit behavior.
findings.verification: Freeze a follow-up artifact that starts immediately after Save and check identity, then proves which downstream records are created, how each can be deleted or superseded, and how later correction remains visible without erasing provenance.

strengths: The frozen r7 surface is intact: every source hash listed in artifact-r7.md recomputed to an exact SHA-256 match against product commit c43145222c7750bf5cfc705384e46ce694f325df before scoring.

The frozen result bundle /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-c431452.xcresult succeeded with 26 passing leaf tests and 0 failures, including RelationshipCaptureTests/testShortcutImporterRejectsBeforeQueueAndReceipt(), RelationshipCaptureTests/testShortcutScreenshotValidatorDecodesContentAndBoundsPayload(), RelationshipCaptureTests/testScreenshotShortcutReceiptRecordsObservedCaptureSeparately(), CandidateSignalUITests/testActionButtonAssignmentAndReceiptStatesRemainIndependent(), CandidateSignalUITests/testActionButtonSetupSeparatesObservedShortcutReceiptFromAssignment(), and CandidateSignalUITests/testPendingScreenshotReviewOffersKeepOrDiscardBeforeProcessing().

r7 resolves the prior medium safety finding with executable proof. apps/ios/Sources/App/CaptureAppIntents.swift:189-203 routes ImportConversationScreenshotIntent through ConversationScreenshotImporter.stage(), and apps/ios/Sources/App/CaptureAppIntents.swift:381-392 validate image content and bounds before PendingCaptureInbox.stage(...) and before TalentSignalSetupPreference.recordScreenshotShortcutReceived(defaults:) records any receipt timestamp.

The new negative-path coverage is specific and sufficient for this release. apps/ios/Tests/RelationshipCaptureTests.swift:7-46 and 48-123 prove corrupt bytes, payloads above 25 MiB, and over-80-megapixel input all fail before queue creation and before the screenshotShortcutReceivedAtKey changes from zero.

The local evidence store remains purpose-bounded and protected. apps/ios/Sources/Services/PendingCaptureInbox.swift:30-52, 65-96, 112-196, and 225-240 implement exact-payload deduplication, explicit per-item removal, complete file protection, backup exclusion, atomic writes, and rollback on partial persistence failure.

The user-visible state now preserves assignment and observed receipt as distinct facts across multiple surfaces. apps/ios/Sources/Features/AppSettingsView.swift:486-500 states that a screenshot received through the Shortcut confirms only the local handoff and does not prove current Action Button assignment; apps/ios/Sources/Features/AgentSourceSettingsView.swift:267-281, apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAgentStudioView.swift, and apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift show Local receipt separately from Assigned, and the r7 screenshots 5638E563-863E-488F-BC6E-5FAA0459495C.png and 23F307C1-00B3-494A-9A40-98FB2F106BAC.png visibly match that separation.

Release App Intents metadata in /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-release-r7-derived/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/TalentSignal.app/Metadata.appintents/extract.actionsdata confirms ImportConversationScreenshotIntent with title Review screenshot, a required screenshot file parameter, background execution, openAppWhenRun false, and no advertised one-step App Shortcut tile for this required-image action.
missing_evidence: A dedicated post-save lifecycle artifact proving deletion or supersession behavior for reviewed capture records, identity cases, compiled wiki output, and any derived canonical state after Save and check identity.

A physical iPhone demonstration of Action Button assignment and press. artifact-r7.md correctly keeps hardware proof outside simulator evidence instead of claiming the simulator as physical-button validation.
open_questions: After reviewed text is explicitly saved, which exact user-visible surface owns later retraction if the conversation turns out to be unauthorized, stale, or identity-confused?

Will the planned post-save lifecycle audit preserve the same separation between observed source, recruiter correction, downstream derivation, and later supersession that r7 now preserves in the import and review stages?

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery
strengths: The r7 packet is frozen and consistent. I recomputed every SHA-256 listed in artifact-r7.md on September 4, 2026 and every listed product, localization, test, and documentation file matched, so the screenshots, source, product commit c431452, and /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-c431452.xcresult describe one stable release candidate.

The core setup remains the lightest honest version of Action Button capture I have seen in this release line. Screenshot 3CCAE38B-A080-47A9-8E02-AA93CEF28919.png shows one dominant task, the exact two-action Shortcut recipe, the local-before-you-decide boundary above the primary control, and an Open Shortcut editor CTA whose label and empty-editor disclosure match AppSettingsView.swift lines 399-440 rather than pretending the app can install a one-press shortcut by itself.

The setup entry stays highly discoverable without hype. Screenshot 9BE3703B-4A2E-41A1-96E3-A75CA7BFD4F0.png places Set up quick capture near the top of Workspace with the neutral One-time setup badge, matching RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift lines 680-696 and 809-841 and preserving calm hierarchy over novelty or sales language.

The status model remains visually honest. Screenshot 5638E563-863E-488F-BC6E-5FAA0459495C.png shows the unchecked I've assigned the Shortcut control still visible above Screenshot received via Shortcuts, while RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift lines 683-694, AgentSourceSettingsView.swift lines 269-283, and AppSettingsView.swift lines 486-499 and 600-614 keep Local receipt distinct from Assigned and describe the receipt as only a local review-queue handoff. The r7 xcresult shows testActionButtonSetupSeparatesObservedShortcutReceiptFromAssignment() and testActionButtonAssignmentAndReceiptStatesRemainIndependent() both passed.

The Chinese AX5 path remains readable and touch-safe across the reviewed hierarchy. Screenshot 23F307C1-00B3-494A-9A40-98FB2F106BAC.png preserves headline, recipe, local-boundary copy, and the primary CTA without clipping or overlap, and CandidateSignalUITests.swift lines 112-130 explicitly assert that the 打开快捷指令编辑器 control is visible, hittable, and at least 44 points high at AX5.

The broader Chinese Agent path now reads more complete without corrupting the capture truth model. Screenshots D5A64D76-0D8D-434A-A558-32A81DE90971.png and A10384E2-31A3-4CB8-9B1C-348D854AB108.png show that the Agent surface can lead into 来源与导入 and then 操作按钮与快捷指令 while keeping device capabilities, file import, and account-connection states distinct. AgentSourceSettingsView.swift lines 267-303 support that separation, and the Action Button row still says 去设置 or Local receipt instead of implying connected hardware state.

Recovery remains calm and explicit before any processing step. Screenshot 5B7E88EB-5F57-4D6A-9567-D4DC36EC8184.png presents Close this review?, Keep for later, and Discard capture before processing, while RelationshipCaptureView.swift lines 264-285 state that keeping preserves the screenshot and reviewed draft for the next app launch. The r7 xcresult shows testPendingScreenshotReviewOffersKeepOrDiscardBeforeProcessing() passed.

The release candidate now carries a documented bare-Debug fallback instead of leaving that launch state ambiguous. Screenshot E6F4EF2F-9485-43C4-BA2E-02AC4E6B9460.png shows a synthetic preview workspace rather than a broken blank or contradictory auth state, and CandidateSignalUITests.swift lines 19-26 explicitly assert editorial-today plus workspace-preview-boundary while authentication-screen remains absent.

The rejection boundary remains proven at the behavior level, not just described in copy. The r7 xcresult shows RelationshipCaptureTests/testShortcutImporterRejectsBeforeQueueAndReceipt() passed, and RelationshipCaptureTests.swift lines 48-123 verify that corrupt, over-25-MiB, and over-80-megapixel inputs create neither a queued capture nor a receipt timestamp.
missing_evidence: This is still evidence level 3 under the mobile-ux-reviewer rubric: I reviewed hash-matched source, screenshots, manifest evidence, and the final xcresult bundle, but I did not directly interact with the live release candidate during this r7 sign-off.

No connected physical iPhone was available on September 4, 2026, so this packet cannot prove real Action Button assignment, hardware press ergonomics, or device-specific failure behavior. I am treating Simulator evidence only as simulator evidence.

The AX5 screenshots and UI assertions are strong for layout and hit targets, but they still do not replace a direct VoiceOver pass for focus order, spoken labels, rotor behavior, and interruption handling on device.

reviews.lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration
strengths: r7 keeps the consent and purpose boundary explicit before fast capture is enabled. artifact-r7.md, hash-matched AppSettingsView.swift, and the fresh English setup screenshot evidence/ui-test-attachments-r7/3CCAE38B-A080-47A9-8E02-AA93CEF28919.png all say to capture only a conversation you are authorized to use, keep the screenshot local until review, and send reviewed text only after Save and check identity.

The receipt state is careful and does not overclaim. The observed receipt screenshot evidence/ui-test-attachments-r7/5638E563-863E-488F-BC6E-5FAA0459495C.png keeps the assignment control unchecked, labels the detail state Screenshot received via Shortcuts, and states that this confirms only the local handoff rather than the current Action Button assignment or a physical press. CandidateSignalUITests.swift asserts the same separation across relaunch states.

Identity uncertainty and user agency remain visible in the review flow. The review screenshot evidence/ui-test-attachments-r7/5B7E88EB-5F57-4D6A-9567-D4DC36EC8184.png and hash-matched RelationshipCaptureView.swift show inspect-original, Keep for later, Discard capture, Speaker unresolved, and Unresolved is a valid result before Save and check identity becomes the next step.

Privacy candor is backed by behavior, not decorative copy. CaptureAppIntents.swift still returns Saved on this iPhone. Nothing was uploaded or confirmed. RelationshipCaptureTests.swift covers rejection before both queue and receipt for corrupt, over-25-MiB, and over-80-megapixel inputs. /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-c431452.xcresult records 26 passed tests for the frozen release candidate.

The surrounding surfaces stay honest about what is and is not real. The neutral setup entry screenshot evidence/ui-test-attachments-r7/9BE3703B-4A2E-41A1-96E3-A75CA7BFD4F0.png keeps this as one-time setup rather than a gamified promise, and the documented bare Debug fallback screenshot evidence/ui-test-attachments-r7/E6F4EF2F-9485-43C4-BA2E-02AC4E6B9460.png shows the product failing into an explicit local preview path instead of pretending live relationship data exists.
missing_evidence: No physical iPhone was connected on 2026-09-04, so a real hardware Action Button assignment and press remain an explicit platform-evidence boundary rather than a proven behavior.

top_findings.next_step: Run a physical-device first-use study without changing the approved setup surface first.
top_findings.verification: A fresh user assigns, captures, and correctly explains the receipt boundary without coaching.

top_findings.reason: The safe local import is complete, but system-wide retraction after explicit save is not part of this artifact.
top_findings.next_step: Create a separate downstream data inventory and deletion/supersession test.

top_findings.reason: Automatic next-launch recovery is proven, while the Settings receipt itself remains informational.
top_findings.next_step: Evaluate a direct oldest-pending-review action only if field observation shows this detour matters.
top_findings.verification: The optional action opens exactly one oldest item without mutating assignment state.

agreements: The exact Take Screenshot → Review screenshot recipe is the lightest truthful setup because iOS keeps Action Button assignment user-owned.
The button press creates protected local pending evidence and performs no hidden network or Agent work.
Assigned and Local receipt are separate truths, and neither claims proof of a physical press.
Human review, identity uncertainty, keep, discard, retry, and no-action remain available before downstream promotion.
r7 resolves the prior medium safety evidence gap with one executable rejection-ordering test.

veto_resolution.veto: A screenshot receipt promoted the user's manual Action Button assignment state in the first review round.
veto_resolution.evidence: r7 writes only the receipt timestamp and CandidateSignalUITests/testActionButtonAssignmentAndReceiptStatesRemainIndependent() passes across all four states and relaunch.

adjudication.rationale: All four selected specialist packets validate against the frozen r7 artifact; scores are 3, 3, 4, and 4 without averaging, and no current veto, blocker, high, or medium finding remains. The product commit is rebased onto v0.1.42, the focused gate passes 26 of 26 tests, and the app-owned capture path, privacy boundary, state truth, recovery, localization, and human authorization gate are directly evidenced. Physical hardware, field comprehension, live VoiceOver, and broader post-save lifecycle governance remain explicitly isolated follow-up evidence rather than false release claims.
